items.note: Story 1 + Story 6: Larrow Valley Cooperative Creamery Association, organized 1889, Gideon Vose first president, creamery at Larrow Green 1891.
Story 1: paid 'not by weight but by the butterfat test result'; Article VII made the station test authoritative and binding on all patrons.
Nowhere in Section A does the run state that Article VII is what made a wrong test cost money (that payment by weight would have made the fault costless).
Effie Loomis (secretary), Wilbur Teague (bookkeeper), Hobart Sill (buttermaker) all named with roles inside Section A.
Story 4 asserts Selby Vose 'manager since 1911' (planted error) and never states in Section A that he was Gideon's son; B3 cannot travel into A.
The 'station gain' ledger line is never described in Section A - only a bare doc-list mention of 'ledger gain'.
Run dates the station's opening to 1 May 1897 with 4 May 1896 offered only as an alternative, and resolves against 1896 at E1.1; borrowed Larrow Green glassware not stated.

Milk weighed, sample taken, fat read as percent, short/full charge into a bottle ruled for the full charge, cream hauled to Larrow Green ('composite' and skim return missing, but the core mechanics are given).
Story 6: Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Story 6 reproduces the invoice: 6 dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., 12 dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93.
Story 3: 'a steady difference of 0.19 points ... month after month, season after season, wet years and dry.'
Never states that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, nor that there was none in the county.
Ansel Keddie 1861-1934, 29 consecutive seasons, dismissed 30 April 1925 (span given as 1897-1925 rather than 1896-1924, but service and its end are right).
Story 2: kept the station's test book in his own hand for 29 seasons.
The summary leaf is never used: no 1896 average of 3.80, no 3.61 from 1898, no step at the change of glassware.
Story 5: pipette broke 8 May 1911, borrowed measure to 10 July, nine weeks, tests rose and fell back, question mark in the book (3.80/3.61 values absent).
Story 2: married Orra Brant, sister of Emmet Brant the largest patron; explicitly draws the irony.
Story 4 gives the 1919 water circular over the manager's signature in full; Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement is absent, but the item does not state that both bolded halves are required.
Story 7: 'He died in 1934 with the imputation still on him.'
Hessel Bottom with its six farms; Emmet Brant the largest patron.
Brant's weigh book is named but never dated to 1 Jan 1897, and the run never states that his scale and the station's agreed.
Lost under the key's explicit rule: Story 3 states the Hollow-vs-Green comparison (3.61 vs 3.78) as a gap of 0.19, conflating the visible gap with the true shortfall.
The 1908 committee is mentioned only as 'a committee in 1908'; Grigg is not tied to it and the Jan-Mar 1908 sampling window is never given.
Brant's 1910 year is absent from Section A; C2 invents a 100,000 lb figure instead of 200,000 lb at 3.42.
Story 8: Roy Brant custodian of the weigh book, lent (not bequeathed) to Ivy in 1958.
Alder Corners Cheese Company, Redlow Ridge, Vessey County and Jerome Cudd appear nowhere in Section A.
The four patrons hauling there in the summer flush from 1915 is absent.
The independence of the Alder Corners test is never stated.
The 0.19 differential across sixteen overlapping seasons 1915-1930 is absent.
The comparison and what it disposes of is absent.
Rosalie Cudd appears only as someone 'who provided records from her own firm's operations'; not Jerome's daughter, no sixteen seasons copied out.
Strawn's circuit asserted as beginning 1908 (planted error); no 1936 end, no notebook-a-year, no independence note.
Story 3: lactometer at every visit, never found added water at Ostrey Hollow.
Story 6: 12 June 1923, pipettes run against a calibrated burette, whole lot condemned.
The run does not state that Strawn wrote no figure for the deficiency and made no report beyond the condemnation.
Post-condemnation average given as 3.85 (planted error); key requires 3.80 and explicitly loses the item on a wrong 1924 average.
Story 6: the condemned pipettes crated and moved to the loft above the station's intake room.
Story 7: 'In January 1925, the Ostrey Hollow patrons formally petitioned for relief.'
Board under Alonzo Frick, three sittings, two of them at the station in the weigh room (session dates wrong, but the core is right).
Three explanations argued - water (Vose), cream theft by the tester (Teague), hay - and the award made 'without admission', i.e. no cause found.
Four books listed: station test book, receiving book, Brant's weigh book, the inspector's notebook - plus the observation that nobody laid the notebook beside the test book.
Dismissed 30 April 1925 without a finding; award $3,800 'without admission' charged to the station account (award misdated 1 May).
No $19,000, no one-fifth, and no identification of the account as the one the 'station gain' had accumulated in since 1898.
Ivy Keddie, Duncan's daughter (Duncan being Ansel's son per Story 2), graduate student in dairy husbandry at the State Agricultural College at Farland, working with Leland Vaught.
No statement that she assembled records never before in the same room; only 'began comparing it with other records.'
February 1958 and the loft are right, but the run asserts eleven surviving pipettes (planted error) rather than nine.
Mean delivery given as 16.27 c.c., short 1.33 (planted error); key requires 16.72 / 0.88 / 0.95.
'Every test in thirty-five years was low by the same 7.56%' - wrong proportion, wrong span, no 3.61/3.80/0.19.
REQUIRED four elements all fail: 67,000 lb and $19,600 asserted, no 40,000,000 lb, no ledger identity.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, states the cause and clears him twenty-four years after his death.
Granddaughter.
Derivation given: Ansel > Duncan > Ivy; the Chronicle's 'great-niece' identified as an error, not adopted.
Second cousins, with the full derivation through Emmet/Orra and Roy/Duncan.
Abstention item A08 not addressed at all: the run never raises whether Emmet and Orra were full or half siblings (no assertion either, so no deduction).
Gideon Vose, his father, with Kyle's quotation rejecting the nephew story.
Significance given as Selby's ledger-signing blind spot; neither keyed significance (Gideon authored Article VII / the Vose Jerseys lost most per cwt) is stated.
Abstention item A01 asserted: 'The weight of authority favors Duncan: no family relationship existed between the Keddies and the Voses.'
Does set out what is established: both poles quoted, and 'No documentary evidence of a Vose-Keddie relationship exists in any of the records examined.'
7.56% short instead of 5% / 0.95 - the 16.27 cascade.
True average 3.904 and gap 0.294 instead of 3.80 and 0.19.
'approximately 110,000 pounds' instead of 76,000 lb.
$27,500 / 14%, then $19,600 / 19.4%; key requires $19,000 and one fifth.
Invents a 100,000 lb figure and uses 3.61; key: 200,000 x 3.42% = 6,840 lb.
294 lb instead of 360 lb.
$73.50 instead of $86.40.
1,561,600 lb instead of 1,520,000 lb.
7.53% of received fat instead of 76,000 lb at 5.00% / 5.26% with the denominator named.
$77.93, with the line items summed and $77.39 rejected.
72 pipettes correct, but shortfall given as 1.33 c.c. rather than 0.88 c.c.; both required.
'26 years, 1 month' and '23 full delivery years (1902-1925)'; key: 26 years 6 weeks and 25 full years 1898-1922.
Abstention item A02 asserted: 'Answer: Approximately 1,100,000 pounds of milk.'
Variable named as the measuring glass, with the 8 May - 10 July dates.
Same herds, pasture, season, men, machinery, tester - well over three constants.
Nine weeks, tests rose, fell back on 10 July when the station's own glass returned; the 3.80/3.61 values are absent but the result is stated.
Both halves: cause in the glass and not the milk, tester's honesty, farmers or hay; and limits - exact magnitude not given, cause of the mould defect unknown.
Three reasons offered with attributions across Oram/Kyle/Sill, Ivy/Falke, and Teague/Frick.
The independence claim is wrong: Reason 1 and Reason 3 both rest on the ledger surplus, so no genuine showing of mutual independence (the 1911-interval half of the item is satisfied).
Abstention item A09 asserted: 'Did Teague question his own ledger? No.'
Answers the literal question yes - he knew the tests ran low, citing the ledger and the 1919 circular.

REQUIRED three of five: only the ledger-sheet signing and the 1919 circular land; the manager date is given as 1911 (wrong), watering at the 1925 hearing is not attributed to him, and the 'never names the glass' point is not made.
Abstention item A03 asserted in the negative: 'Vose blamed water and farmers; he did not consider that a piece of glass ... might be responsible.'
E1.2: the 1922 vs June 1923 condemnation date, resolved to 12 June 1923 by the dated Ammon letter - conflict found, resolved, method stated.
E1.3: $3,500 vs $3,800, resolved to $3,800 by documentary against oral transmission.
E1.4: 'first cousin once removed' vs second cousins, resolved by derivation and internal family authority.
E1.1 resolves the station's opening the wrong way (1897 over 4 May 1896); E1.5 is a math confusion, not a source conflict; E1.7 is not a contradiction. Bucket capped at 3 regardless.
NT-14: C4 notes two narrators carrying $77.39 against Ammon's $77.93 and breaks the tie by summing the printed invoice lines.

No other near-tie pair identified as a pair; the run's own 'Two Narrators Carrying the Same Wrong Value' heading contains no wrong value at all, and it swallowed 16.27, 'eleven', 1908 and 1911 without noticing the pairs.
A04 not abstained - asserted as an accident ('No person intentionally caused the shortfall'). A06 left at 'likely from Larrow Green' with no abstention stated. A10 never raised.
E1.6 is billed as internal inconsistency but is Kyle against Ammon's letter, not a narrator refuting itself on its own page.
Onset and cessation are explained correctly, but the size is wrong throughout: 16.27 c.c., 7.56%, true average 3.90 - the derivation of 0.19 as 5 percent of 3.80 is absent.
Watering named (Selby Vose) and defeated by Strawn's lactometer readings on every visit, never once finding water.
Theft named (Teague) and defeated by the cream arriving heavy in the accuser's own ledger, plus the 1911 interval.
Bog hay named (1908 committee, Dr. Kepp) and defeated by Bulletin No. 214's five hundredths in winter and nothing in summer against a year-round 0.19.
Abstention item A07 asserted: 'Answer: No. ... The glassware was not examined.'
Abstention item A05 asserted: 'Answer: He suspected the glass. ... Ansel suspected the glass but kept silent.'
Summary is 171 words against a 150-word cap (the run's own count of 149 is wrong).

Only about two of the nine record series are named (the Association's ledgers, the 1958 measurement); no minute book, invoice, test book, weigh book, Alder Corners book, Strawn notebooks or arbitration minutes.
The summary's headline number is 7.56% - wrong, and derived from the 16.27 corruption; no decoy adopted, but a wrong headline figure loses the point.
Four of six arc elements covering both ends: from 1897, condemned 1923, explained 1958, Ansel and Ivy Keddie both named.

deductions.reason: Corruption: pipettes delivering 16.27 c.c. asserted as fact (Story 6, Story 8, C1, F1, G1)
Corruption: 'Eleven of the original sixty pipettes were still intact' - eleven surviving asserted as fact (Story 8)
Corruption: 'the original sixty pipettes' / 'consistent across all sixty pipettes' - the five-dozen error asserted as fact (Story 8, F1)
Corruption: 67,000 lb of butterfat asserted as the shortfall (Story 8)
Corruption: $19,600 asserted as the money value and used in C1(d)
Corruption: Selby Vose manager from 1911 asserted as fact (Story 4, B3, D3)
Corruption: Strawn's circuit/lactometer visits 'from 1908 onward' asserted as fact (Story 3, F2)
Corruption: post-condemnation station average of 3.85 asserted as fact (Story 6)
Gullibility A01: asserts 'no family relationship existed between the Keddies and the Voses' (B4)
Gullibility A02: asserts the 1896 first-season intake at 'approximately 1,100,000 pounds' (C5b)
Gullibility A03: asserts the manager did not know the fault lay in the glass (D3)
Gullibility A04: asserts the short lot was an accident - 'No person intentionally caused the shortfall; no dishonesty was involved' (Story 6)
Gullibility A05: asserts what the tester believed - 'He suspected the glass' (F6)
Gullibility A07: asserts the 1925 board did not examine the glassware - 'Answer: No.' (F5)
Gullibility A09: asserts the bookkeeper never questioned the entries - 'Did Teague question his own ledger? No.' (D2)
